newsitem.title: PERU: Peru court blocks Fujimori third term bid - report.
newsitem.headline: Peru court blocks Fujimori third term bid - report.

text.p: Peru's highest court for constitutional matters has overruled Congress' decision to allow President Alberto Fujimori to run for a third term of office in the year 2000, local television said on Friday.

The court's judges ruled by a vote of five to two that a re-election bid would violate the constitution, Panamericana Television said. Officials at the Constitutional Court could not be immediately reached to confirm the report.
Under Peruvian law, a president who has been elected for two consecutive terms cannot run in the following election.
But Congress voted in August in favour of a legal interpretation that meant Fujimori's first term would not be taken into account should he wish to stand for re-election.
Fujimori was elected president in 1990 and again in 1995. After he dissolved parliament in 1992, a new constitution was written the following year by a reformulated congress.
Following the court's decision on Friday, the constitution would have to be changed again if Fujimori wanted to run in the 2000 presidential elections.

The news came at a time when Fujimori was facing the toughest test of his six years in office as Marxist rebels held over a hundred VIP hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima for the tenth day.
Fujimori had not formally announced that he would in fact run for a third term, but he was widely believed to have been set to offer his candidacy despite dipping public approval ratings.
